_note: Design v0.2. Modules and deliverables come from the Ain Foundry Roadmap and the 'EIR mentoring and advising responsibilities' document Roberto showed on 2026-10-22. Step numbers refer to Bill Aulet's Disciplined Entrepreneurship (24 steps). Key questions and required evidence rungs are our initial standard; they are calibrated by AIN EIRs reviewing the first judgments. Each question's 'step' is a draft mapping to one of the 24 steps (0 = a Foundry item outside the 24 steps), to confirm with Roberto.

rungs.2: Desk research: reports, web data, AI estimates (verify before relying on them)
rungs.4: Customers did: sign-ups, letters of intent, time spent, switching
rungs.6: Retained behavior: repeat purchase, renewal, continued use

modules.title: Business Model Canvas
modules.focus: Is the problem real, for whom exactly, and what business model might serve them? Push for customer discovery before anything is polished.

deliverables.title: Customer discovery

questions.ask: Which specific group is your first (beachhead) market, and why this one rather than the others?
What problem do they have, and how do you know it is real and painful for them?
How do they solve it today, and what does that cost them?
How many people have you interviewed, and what did they actually do, not just say?
Can you name your next 10 potential customers?

consider: Estimate the size of your beachhead market (step 4) and say where each number comes from.
Write a persona of one real person you interviewed (step 5).
Look for a bigger or more painful group you have not considered yet.

deliverables.title: Business Model Canvas

questions.ask: Is the person who uses it the same as the person who pays? If not, who pays, and why would they?
Can you quantify the value: how much time, money or risk does it save the customer?
How will customers find out about it and get it?
How will you make money? Mark it as a guess if you have not tested a price yet.
What are the main costs of delivering it?

consider: Mark every canvas block that is still a guess; the Virtual EIR will come back to them in Module 3.
Walk through the full life cycle: how a customer discovers, buys, installs, uses and pays (step 6).

modules.title: The Perfect Pitch
modules.focus: Who decides to buy, why you and not a competitor, and has anyone committed? Act like the toughest investor in the room.

deliverables.title: Pitch deck (slides and practice)
steps: 13 Process to acquire a paying customer
23 Show the dogs will eat the dog food

questions.ask: Who decides on the purchase, who influences it, and who can block it?
Who else solves this, and what do you have that they cannot easily copy?
Has anyone paid, pre-ordered or signed a letter of intent?
What are the steps to get one paying customer, and how long do they take?
Which legal structure do you plan, and who advised you? (A human EIR handles the legal advice.)
Where have you pitched it, and what was the hardest question you got?

consider: Record a video of your pitch; Ain asks for practice, not only slides.
Run a mock investor Q&A with the Virtual EIR before the next competition.
Define the smallest product a customer would pay for (step 22).

modules.title: The Business Plan
modules.focus: Every number needs a source. Stress-test the plan like an investor: unit economics, deployment, funding.

deliverables.title: Business plan

questions.ask: What is your price, and where does that number come from?
What is a customer worth over time, and what does it cost to acquire one?
Which key assumptions have you tested, and what happened?
What happens to the plan if conversion is half of what you expect?
Who installs or deploys it at the customer, and what could block that (for example their IT team)?
How much money do you need, for which milestone, and from which source? (Term sheets go to a human EIR.)

consider: Name your follow-on markets and how big they are (step 14).
Enter a business plan competition to test the plan in front of judges.
Ask a human EIR about any financing offer before you accept it.

alumni.title: Graduated to NextCorps
alumni.focus: All Ain EIRs agreed the venture is ready for the next accelerator.

chain: Be specific: who exactly, how many, when?
Evidence: how do you know? Did customers say it, do it, or pay for it?
Alternatives: how do they cope today? Is there a bigger or more painful group? Who else is doing this?
Consequence: if this is wrong, what happens to your venture?
Test: what is the smallest test this week, and what result would prove you wrong?
